palette.notes: Clips: pastel grounds (mint, pink, peach) with warm wood browns and orange cones; one teal-and-cream cottage. Shadow faces are darker, slightly redder browns; outlines are dark navy or brown.

lighting: Three-face lighting on every block: top face lightest, one side mid, the other side darkest, light from the upper left. A darker floor tile under objects acts as a contact shadow.
silhouette: Everything is built from 2:1 cuboids (shelves, tables, cones, a house): the readable shape is the diamond top plus two side faces; small props stack inside bigger ones.

motion.timing: Clips show placement and build-up, not character animation: objects snap onto the grid, stack, and a drawing is built line by line in a sped-up timelapse.

texture: Flat fills per face with a few lighter planks or tile seams; the cottage adds roof shingles, half-timbering and stone at the end. Faces are meant to tile seamlessly on all four sides.
camera: Fixed dimetric view with no perspective, so objects keep their size anywhere on the grid; the camera only pushes in on one object or pulls out to a full room.

acting.enters: No characters; props pop onto a tile (shelf, then a second, third) or a cursor drops them in.
acting.acts: Stacking and nesting: items go inside shelves, cones on top, chair on the table, until a whole cluttered room is built.
acting.depth: Depth comes from the grid: things further up-screen are further back, and overlap does the rest, not scale.

techniques: 2:1 two-step lines (about 26.5 degrees) instead of true 30 degrees
three-face shading: light top, mid left, dark right
build objects from cuboids on a wireframe guide, then sculpt details
even tile sizes so faces tile seamlessly
contact shadow tile under each object
build-up reveal: line art, flat colours, shading, texture, background
feel: pastel ground + warm three-face cubes + objects snapping onto a 2:1 grid = cozy toybox diorama
for_fred: For a product-feature beat, put Fred on a small isometric tile island and have features pop onto tiles around him one at a time, each snapping in with a contact shadow. Avoid: isometric gives no scale for depth, so if Fred must go 'far away', move him up-screen behind props instead of shrinking him.
